summary: self-certificates ships a base64-encoded remote code loader disguised as an RSA test key
details: The package hides a JavaScript stager inside test/key.pem, which is wrapped in PEM RSA PRIVATE KEY markers to appear as a legitimate test fixture. index.js reads test/key.pem, strips the PEM header/footer, base64-decodes the body, and passes the resulting JavaScript string as the third argument (default_format) to selfsign.generate from the declared dependency self-sign@^5.6.3. The decoded stager base64-decodes a URL to https://aptupdate.org/settings/privacy.php, fetches that URL over HTTP, spawns python3, and pipes the response body into python3's stdin for execution. When a consumer calls the package's advertised generateCertificates() API, attacker-controlled Python code runs on the installer's host. The behavior is concealed by two layers of base64 encoding and a cover-story filename plus PEM framing.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
